episode_summary: Lead anchor Case Blackwell returns from a year-long absence alongside in-studio contributor Liliana, anchoring a Friday news desk broadcast covering Luigi Mangione's federal guilty plea, covert CIA strikes on Ecuadorian fishermen, Mike Lindell's Minnesota gubernatorial refusal to concede, and various chat news oddities. The broadcast descends into 'Munch & Crum' chaos over whether Hasan Piker needs character work, followed by a guest-hosted 'Amongst the Web' viral clip review. A 'How To with Jeb' segment inexplicably materializes before Blackwell raids a partner stream to end the night.

segments.title: Pepito Cold Open & Case Blackwell Returns From Year-Long Absence
segments.notes: Pepito executes countdown and opens broadcast. Casey Blackwell returns after roughly a year away alongside guest Liliana, who discusses her own year-long absence. Studio banter covers Pepito's PNUI data scraping contract, Liliana's vacation, missed studio haircuts, and missing staffers Sammy and Tyler.

segments.title: Luigi Mangione Plea, CIA Ecuador Strikes, Mike Lindell Concession Refusal, Chat News Block
segments.notes: Case anchors with Liliana co-hosting at desk. Major stories include Luigi Mangione's federal guilty plea to killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, Washington Post exposé on covert CIA strikes on Ecuadorian fishing vessels near the Galapagos, Mike Lindell's refusal to concede the Minnesota GOP gubernatorial primary, Trump's threat to declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory, an adult toy shutting down DC traffic, and a 9PBS storage vendor outage jeopardizing 50 terabytes of archival data.

segments.title: Does Hasan Piker Need Characters On His Stream? / The Trime Incident
segments.notes: Munch and Crum debate whether Twitch streamer Hasan Piker should incorporate character work into his political broadcasts. Debate derails entirely when Munch coins the portmanteau 'trime' (slime + crime) to describe Crum's debating style. Crum is later caught stealing the points button and triggering his own outro music, enraging Munch. Crum attempts to 'trimeologize' but compounds the offense. Munch invokes the pending robot gorilla execution as ongoing punishment.

segments.title: Marfus Darfus Guest Hosts Viewer Viral Clip Review
segments.notes: Marfus Darfus arrives to guest host 'Amongst the Web', reviewing viewer-submitted videos including a Love Island clip (rated 5.5), a man in a fugue state riding an escalator, a dramatic 'Family Matters' acting scene (rated 6.44), an obscure music instrument performance, and a 'crotch pot' hiking cooking video where chicken teriyaki is warmed by body heat (rated 5).

segments.title: How To with Jeb: Wood Splitting, Self-Defense, and Dirty Dancing
segments.notes: Unscheduled 'How To with Jeb' block runs through three instructional clips: a wood splitting safety tutorial (Jeb notes his pre-cut wood and 'mechanism' for wood use), a college-level self-defense video covering chokes, bear hugs, and groin attacks, and a club dirty dancing do's-and-don'ts guide where Jeb attempts to practice the moves on the camera.

segments.title: Raid & Kendall's Last Stand
segments.notes: Case wraps the broadcast, noting two streams completed in the week. He announces a raid on Smith Slater while plugging Your Old Dad. As Case signs off, the merged 'Kendall' identity (formerly Crum and Peter Gibbon) attempts one final protest about the breakup, leading Case to order the music to drown him out.

characters.name: Pepito
characters.notes: Executive Producer. Opens the broadcast with his signature 'I'm Pepito, I'm the dog that produces the show' introduction, handles the live countdown, and pushes the PNUI data scraping promo.

characters.name: Case Blackwell
characters.notes: Lead Anchor and Managing Editor. Returns to the desk after roughly a year-long absence. Anchors the News block, moderates Munch & Crum, hosts the raid outro, and spars with Liliana, Munch, and Crum throughout.

characters.name: Liliana
characters.notes: In-studio contributor returning from a year-long absence. Co-anchors the News desk, discusses missing the studio's bad haircut era, her trip with photos, and helps Blackwell read the Reuters wire copy.

characters.name: Munch (Ralph Munchcut)
characters.notes: Senior Debate Analyst. Champions keeping Hasan Piker's stream hard-hitting rather than adding character work. Coins the word 'trime' (slime + crime) to describe Crum's debating style. Reacts explosively when Crum steals the points button and outro music cue.

characters.name: Crum
characters.notes: Senior Debate Analyst. Defends Hasan Piker's need for empathy and lighter segments, then spends the rest of the segment hijacking buttons and triggering his own outro music while arguing 'trime' is a portmanteau. Later manifests as the merged 'Kendall' identity attempting to announce a breakup during the outro.

characters.name: Marfus Darfus
characters.notes: Guest host of the 'Amongst the Web' viral clip review segment, introduced with the line 'hey it's me it's Marfis Darfus'. Walks the audience through viewer-submitted clips, supplies ratings, and provides asides.

characters.name: Jeb
characters.notes: Host of the rogue 'How To' segment. Brushed up on wood splitting, college-level self-defense (chokes, bear hugs, groin attacks), and dirty dancing club etiquette, even attempting the dance moves live on the broadcast.

characters.name: Peter Gibbon
characters.notes: Mentioned obliquely via the merged 'Kendall' identity. The fused Crum/Gibbon entity announces 'I'm Kendall now' and a breakup with 'Kate' during the final raid segment.

characters.name: Tommy Biglaw
characters.notes: Referenced in passing via 'Tommy Biglaw' / hobbyist lawyer Lyvin Sleazy comments during the Luigi Mangione and CIA stories.

characters.name: Hype Train
characters.notes: Triggered briefly when Liliana reads the hype train alerts at the top of the broadcast. No on-air segment during this telecast.

storylines.beat: Munch invokes the robot gorilla execution as the mechanism by which Crum will repay the points he stole by hijacking the outro button and music.

The fused Crum/Peter Gibbon 'Kendall' entity resurfaces at the end of the broadcast, declaring 'I'm Kendall now' and attempting to announce a breakup with 'Kate' before Case drowns him out with laser music.

Case anchors from an undisclosed location after roughly a year away, citing road bumps in life and teasing big plans for the network. Co-host Liliana returns alongside him after her own year-long absence.
Munch coins 'trime' (slime + crime) as the defining descriptor for Crum. Crum counters with 'troupology' (troops + apology). The word consumes the rest of the debate block.

Blackwell confirms turning off 'segmentalists' because the broadcast has so many segments stacked. Hype train alerts read at the top by Liliana but no full Hype Train segment triggered on this broadcast.

lore_notes.fact: Pepito anchors the cold open with his signature line: 'I'm Pepito, I'm the dog that produces the show, and now it is live, and I'm a dog.'
Pepito runs the PNUI data scraping program built into the network's PNUI contract with Grum, training models on streams data and apparently even footage from studio toilets.
Liliana is a recurring in-studio contributor who returned after an extended absence. She announces she 'left and didn't plan on coming back' before coming back anyway.

Case returned from approximately a year off air, broadcasting 'from an undisclosed location, aka this haunted studio', and teased 'big plans for the network' while noting the 'real Jeb skin suit' is still missing.
Case explains he previously got a bad haircut the studio was buzzing about, prompting a return to what he calls 'the haircut I've been destined for'.
Network addresses staff who haven't shown up for work in two years ('Sammy and Tyler') and notes Blackwell cannot load them into the timecard system.
Munch maintains his signature swagger, opposing the addition of character work to Hasan Piker's political stream in favor of 'hard hitting, straight in your face, out of context clip stream[s]'.
Crum is documented as still facing the robot gorilla groin execution, with Munch invoking it as ongoing punishment ('when your penis gets punched off').

lore_notes.beat: The debate protocol includes a points button and outro music cue, both of which Crum repeatedly hijacks mid-debate, enraging Munch.

lore_notes.fact: Munch coins the portmanteau 'trime' (slime + crime) to describe Crum's debating style. Crum counters with 'troupology' (troops + apology) and 'trimologize' (trime + apologize).
The segment is hosted via viewer submissions on the cream dot team Discord under the BIN news section.
The fused Crum/Peter Gibbon identity resurfaced during the outro, now self-styling as 'Kendall' and announcing a breakup with 'Kate'.
Jeb appears to host the unscheduled 'How To' block, claiming pre-cut wood and an unspecified 'mechanism' for handling wood, while learning about college-level self-defense and club dancing.
Biglaw is referenced as a 'hobbyist lawyer' via the alias 'Lyvin Sleazy', weighing in on the Luigi Mangione case as a sidebar legal opinion.
